exposure: Microbial isolates (Group B streptococci, Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CONS), Enterococci, Klebsiella, Enterobacter)
outcome: Antibiotic susceptibility (ampicillin, gentamicin, vancomycin, cefotaxime, cloxacillin)
cohort: The study included 5249 infants admitted to a level-four neonatal intensive care unit in Norway, from whom 287 infants with 324 positive blood cultures for sepsis were identified.
finding: Empiric treatment with ampicillin and gentamicin was adequate for early-onset sepsis, while combining vancomycin and gentamicin may be a safer alternative to cefotaxime for late-onset sepsis.
